title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problemStatement: Given a string s, find the longest palindromic substring in s. You may assume that the maximum length of s is 1000.

examples.explanation: "aba" is also a valid answer, but "bab" is equally long.

approaches.name: Brute Force Approach
algorithm: Initialize variables to track the start and end indices of the longest palindrome found so far.
Iterate through all possible starting indices `i` (from 0 to N-1).
Iterate through all possible ending indices `j` (from `i` to N-1). This defines a substring `s[i...j]`.
For each substring, check if it is a palindrome by comparing `s[k]` and `s[l]` moving inwards from the ends (`k=i`, `l=j`). This takes O(j-i) time.
If the substring is a palindrome and its length (`j - i + 1`) is greater than the current maximum length, update the longest palindrome indices.

approaches.name: Optimal Approach: Expand Around Center
algorithm: Initialize variables to store the start index (`start`) and maximum length (`maxLength`) of the longest palindrome found.
A string of length N has 2N - 1 possible centers: N single characters (for odd length palindromes) and N-1 spaces between characters (for even length palindromes).
Iterate through all possible centers `i` from 0 to N-1.
For each center `i`, call a helper function `expand(s, left, right)` twice: once for odd length palindromes (center `i, i`) and once for even length palindromes (center `i, i+1`).
The `expand` function checks characters outward from `left` and `right`, decrementing `left` and incrementing `right` as long as `s[left] == s[right]` and they remain within bounds.
After expansion stops, calculate the current palindrome length (`right - left - 1`).
If the current length is greater than `maxLength`, update `maxLength` and the `start` index accordingly.
